intro.title: Eight examples. Not the whole list.
points: What follows are examples of what this makes possible
All of them are built from the same handful of blocks, combined differently
Which combination fits depends on what you are working on

mix.title: Compute what you can. Ask what you must.
points: Shell steps are free, fast, and identical every time
Put a model only where judgment is needed — per step
The run log tells you which step was which

trace.title: Watch it run. Then read it back.
points: Follow every step live, then step through it afterwards
Each edit to a flow is a version you can restore
Export the whole thing as a process diagram

notice.title: What you notice doesn't evaporate.
points: Side findings become tracked items, not lost thoughts
An item can trigger the work itself, then close when it's verified
Jump back into the session that created it

wait.title: Waiting isn't failing.
points: Pause for an approval, an input, or until tomorrow
It resumes where it stopped — not from the top
Missed schedules get picked up after a restart

verdict.title: A verdict with a half-life.
points: Accept a risk once, with a reason and the evidence behind it
If the evidence degrades, the finding comes back on its own
Six months later it's on your desk again

refill.title: Build the frame once. It keeps filling.
points: New material is merged in, not piled on
Expired entries drop out by themselves
Topics rotate, so nothing sits untouched

swap.title: Swap the model, keep the flow.
points: Run the same flow on a different provider — per step if you want
Model names come from your machine, not a hard-coded list
Put two providers on one flow and compare

blocks.title: Everything is a building block.
points: A whole flow can be one step inside another
Chains line up finished flows end to end
Loops, branches, retries and approvals are blocks like any other

closing.title: This tour was built by the thing it's showing you.
points: The texts, the images and this sequence come from workflows in the pool
Install one of them, run it, and read the log
